subject: Discovery Recap: Tool/Function Calling & Structured Output Requirements
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Singh <priya@datastruct.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Tool/Function Calling & Structured Output Requirements

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our 30-min discovery to make sure we captured the right priorities and next steps. Please reply with edits or missing items.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Multiple internal tools and knowledge bases; current orchestration for agents is brittle and non-deterministic.
- Outputs from the agent layer are inconsistent (free-text vs structured), which breaks downstream integrations.
- Hard to trace which external tools (ticketing, billing, search) were invoked and with what args; auditability and observability are limited.

Current stack you described:
- Home-grown agent controller + a few microservices (Python/Flask)
- External tools: Zendesk, Snowflake, internal KB (Confluence)
- Hosting: GCP (us-west1), no dedicated inference infra today

Success criteria you enumerated:
- Deterministic, schema-validated structured output for all tool calls (JSON-first contract).
- Clear agent workflows with explicit tool-call logs and idempotent replays.
- <1s median tooling call latency where possible; predictable failure modes and fallbacks.
- Strong formatting/validation guarantee: model must return parseable JSON matching provided JSON Schema with clear error codes when schema validation fails.

What we (Redwood) proposed:
- Use function/tool-calling primitives plus a JSON Schema enforcement layer.
- Option to pin a strict schema for critical agent outputs (e.g., ticket create payload) and a relaxed schema for exploratory prompts.
- Instrumentation: per-token cost/latency + per-tool-call audit trail + KV/prefix caching for repeated workflows.

Immediate next steps:
1) I will share a draft JSON Schema and an example agent workflow doc (link below).
2) Technical deep-dive meeting (30-45m) with your engineers + our SE (Dev Patel) to walk through schema edge cases and error-handling.
3) Security/compliance follow-up: you asked for SOC2 and data-retention details — we'll attach the questionnaire and SOC2 pointer.

Deliverables we committed to:
- Draft JSON Schema for two common flows: ticket.create and search.query (by EOD tomorrow).
- Action plan PDF with milestones and timeline (attached).

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

Attachments: acme-action-plan.pdf

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@datastruct.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Tool/Function Calling & Structured Output Requirements

Jordan — thanks for the detailed recap. This looks right to me; appreciate the concrete next steps. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) Success metric: in addition to schema validation, we'd like a deterministic signal that our downstream processor accepts >=95% of tool-call payloads without human correction during the first 30 days post-rollout. Can we instrument that?
2) Example edge case: our ticket.create needs an optional `escalationLevel` integer and a `customerId` that must match our internal 12-char hex format. We'll need schema-level regex validation and meaningful error payloads when the model violates the format.
3) Security: please attach SOC2 summary and your data retention policy. Also include the person who owns the DPA/contract discussions for procurement.

We'll review the draft schema when you send it. If possible, include an example of a failed validation response from Redwood so we can see how our agents would handle it.

—Samir
Head of AI Platforms, Acme Analytics
samir.k@acme-analytics.com

Attachments requested: acme-security-questions.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-analytics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Tool/Function Calling & Structured Output Requirements

Samir — looping in Dev Patel (SE) to lead the technical deep-dive. Dev, Jordan has a draft schema in flight; please review the Google Doc and propose a time next week for a 45-min session focused on schema edge cases and error semantics.

A few notes from me:
- We can add metrics to track "first-pass acceptance" for downstream processors (95% target is reasonable as an initial SLO).
- For schema enforcement, we typically support: strict validation + structured error responses (error_code, field_errors, suggested_fix) so clients can programmatically decide to retry, sanitize, or send to human review.
- Procurement/contract owner: copying me — I'll coordinate the DPA/Procurement thread and connect your procurement lead to our legal ops (Laura B handles enterprise deals).

I've attached a short action plan and timeline; Jordan will follow up with the draft schema.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-action-plan.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-analytics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Tool/Function Calling & Structured Output Requirements

Thanks — I will take point on the technical deep-dive. I'll post a Doodle and propose Wed/Thu next week for a 45-min slot.

In the meantime, Jordan: can you drop the draft JSON Schema link and one example of a failing validation (what our API would return) into the Google Doc? I want to pre-annotate a few real-world agent prompts so we can test deterministic formatting and error-handling patterns.

—Dev
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
thread_snippet: Recap: deterministic JSON schema for tool calls, agent workflows, next steps: draft schema + technical deep-dive + SOC2/questions
